data.summary: E084 experiment: view-count principle on industrial equipment fault codes (PLC/SCADA). Key results: G1 PASS (30≥30 both arms), G2 FAIL (0.60 accuracy vs 0.85 threshold), G3 REPORTING: treatment 40.0% served (12/30), 20% partially_served (6/30), 40% unserved (12/30); control 56.7% served (17/30), 36.7% partially_served (11/30), 6.7% unserved (2/30). Key differentiator: 20% partially_served rate for industrial equipment PLC/SCADA codes, continuing the gradient pattern across all five tested domains: lab instruments 0%, medical devices 1%, aviation 10%, industrial 20%, general computer errors 36.7%. This establishes a clear dose-response gradient where partially_served rate increases as domains become less code-structured. G4 FAIL (12/20 top-arrival vs threshold 17/20). Four of four priority domains from STATE-next-actions.md now tested, establishing the view-count principle's generalization boundaries across technical/non-software domains. Decision: hold - principle generalizes across all tested domains with systematic domain-differentiated classification patterns; fresh observation needed in new domain per D083.
